kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Super Starter Kit

identity.manufacturer: Texas Instruments (this exact chip is second-sourced by many fabs; ELEGOO does not disclose which one is bundled)
identity.manufacturer_part_number: SN74HC595N (TI's PDIP-16 part number; other manufacturers' 74HC595 parts are pin- and function-compatible)

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A chip that turns 3 wires from the UNO into 8 separate on/off outputs, so you can control 8 LEDs (or more) without using up 8 of the UNO's own pins.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Driving multiple LEDs or other simple digital loads (like 7-segment displays) from just 3 UNO pins; several 74HC595 chips can be chained together for even more outputs.
function.how_it_works_briefly: You send it 8 bits one at a time on the data pin, pulsing the clock pin each time. Once all 8 bits are in, a pulse on the latch pin copies them all to the 8 output pins at once, so nothing flickers while new data is loading.

pinout.name: QH'
pinout.notes: carries the overflow bit; connect to the SER pin of the next 74HC595 when chaining chips

pinout.name: SRCLR
pinout.notes: tie HIGH (to VCC) if not used, so the register is never accidentally cleared

pinout.name: SRCLK
pinout.notes: pulse to shift each new data bit in; ELEGOO's own kit tutorial wires this to UNO Digital 9

pinout.name: RCLK
pinout.notes: pulse after 8 bits are shifted in to move them to the outputs; ELEGOO's own kit tutorial wires this to UNO Digital 11

pinout.name: OE
pinout.notes: tie to GND to keep outputs always enabled; can be PWM'd for brightness control

pinout.name: SER
pinout.notes: the incoming data bit stream; ELEGOO's own kit tutorial wires this to UNO Digital 12

pinout.name: VCC
pinout.notes: 2V to 6V supply; typically wired to the UNO's 5V pin

pins.pin_1_identification: With the small U-shaped notch at the top of the chip, pin 1 (QB) is the top-left pin; pin numbers then run counter-clockwise around the package.

electrical.typical_current: quiescent supply current (ICC) is very low, max 80 microamps with no output loaded
electrical.max_current: each output (QA-QH) can source or sink about 6 mA at 4.5V VCC, rated to drive up to 15 LSTTL loads
electrical.logic_level: 5V CMOS (VIH about 3.15V min, VIL about 1.35V max at VCC=4.5V)

key_specs.max_clock_frequency: up to about 25 MHz at VCC=4.5V
key_specs.chainable: yes, via QH' (pin 9) to the next chip's SER pin

visual_identification.shape_and_size: Black rectangular plastic chip with 16 pins in two rows of 8, a standard 0.3-inch-wide DIP package about 19mm long.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Black plastic body printed with '74HC595' plus a manufacturer logo and date code; a small notch or dimple marks the pin-1 end.
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: 74HC595 (sometimes prefixed, e.g. SN74HC595N or CD74HC595E, depending on the manufacturer)
easily_confused_with: L293D (same 16-pin DIP body size and colour; distinguishable only by the printed part number)
other 74-series logic chips in the same size DIP package

example_connections.uno_pin: GND (tied low to keep outputs always on)
5V/VCC (tied high so the register is never cleared)

wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: none required for the basic lesson (uses plain shiftOut()); the SPI library can be used instead if SER/SRCLK are wired to the UNO's hardware MOSI/SCK pins

hazards: None significant; a low-voltage logic chip
handling_notes: Handle by the edges; CMOS inputs are sensitive to static discharge (rated for 2000V HBM ESD)
Insert with the notch oriented correctly; a chip placed backwards across a breadboard's centre gap will short VCC to GND pins
common_mistakes: Forgetting to tie OE (pin 13) low, which leaves all outputs in a high-impedance 'off' state
Leaving SRCLR (pin 10) floating or low, which keeps clearing the shift register
Mixing up the latch (RCLK) and clock (SRCLK) pins, which are easy to swap since they sit next to each other

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: No LEDs light up at all
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: OE (pin 13) is not tied to GND, or VCC/GND is not connected
symptoms_and_causes.check: Measure DC voltage between pin 16 and pin 8 with a multimeter; it should read about 5V

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: LEDs flicker or show garbage patterns
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: SRCLR (pin 10) is floating instead of tied to VCC
symptoms_and_causes.check: Confirm pin 10 has a solid connection to 5V, not just resting near it on the breadboard

symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: A bad jumper wire or a burnt-out LED/resistor, not usually the chip itself
symptoms_and_causes.check: Swap the suspect LED and resistor to another known-good output pin and see if the fault follows

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: With the board powered, use DC voltage mode to probe pin 16 (VCC) to pin 8 (GND) and confirm about 5V. Then probe each Q output pin to GND while a test sketch drives that output on; a driven-high output should read close to VCC, a driven-low output close to 0V.
